summary: Client priority header mismatch causing intermittent 429s during multipart uploads
description:
Issue summary:
SignalForge reports spikes of 429 responses during large multipart upload jobs that use HTTP/2 with client-supplied priority headers. Failures are intermittent: many parts succeed, but a subset of parallel part uploads receive 429s and abort the overall batch.

Impact:
- Customer's nightly dataset imports (10s of thousands of parts) see 10-20% part-level rejections, causing retries and missed SLAs.
- Occurs in production (us-west) starting 2026-03-11 23:00 PDT after customer rolled out an SDK update that attaches an "x-client-priority" header.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod-us-west) behind edge proxy cluster ep-usw-3.
- Customer uses HTTP/2 multiplexed connections with 16 concurrent streams per connection.
- Upload workflow: multipart PUTs with 8 parallel part uploads per job.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Establish an HTTP/2 connection to https://api.redwood.ai with Authorization: Bearer <key>.
2) For each part upload, send header "x-client-priority: background" for telemetry parts or "x-client-priority: interactive" for small parts.
3) Start 8 parallel part uploads per job across 3 simultaneous jobs (24 concurrent streams).
4) Observe that 2-5 of the streams receive 429 responses within the first 30s of the job.

Observed behavior:
- 429s arrive with response headers: X-Request-ID, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: <timestamp>.
- Server logs show the requests being attributed to the route '/v1/uploads/multipart' but using different internal priority buckets.
- Rejections are clustered when a mix of "interactive" and "background" x-client-priority values are present on the same connection.

Expected behavior:
- Priority headers should be advisory for observability and not cause cross-route token-bucket starvation leading to 429s for well-behaved concurrent uploads.

Customer-provided logs (sanitized):
- Request sample (success):
  :method: PUT
  :path: /v1/uploads/multipart/part
  authorization: Bearer ***
  x-client-priority: interactive
  x-upload-part: 12/1024
  x-request-id: sf-req-20321
- Request sample (429):
  :method: PUT
  :path: /v1/uploads/multipart/part
  authorization: Bearer ***
  x-client-priority: background
  x-upload-part: 23/1024
  x-request-id: sf-req-20347
  response-status: 429
  response-headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0; X-RateLimit-Reset: 2026-03-12T07:02:10Z

Temporary mitigation requested by customer:
- Guidance to avoid 429s while retaining client-side prioritization for telemetry.

Attachments from customer:
- a short pcap and HTTP/2 stream index mapping (uploaded to S3 and linked in comments).

Next steps requested:
- Clarify whether our rate-limiter considers x-client-priority in token accounting, and if so how to prevent mixed-priority starvation on multiplexed connections.
- Recommend configuration or SDK changes that avoid production 429s without losing the customer's internal priority signals.
comments: 2026-03-12 17:05 UTC - Support (Asha Patel): Thanks for the report — we've triaged and assigned to eng. Can you confirm a sample failing request ID (you provided sf-req-20347) and the exact SDK version? Also upload the pcap to the case. We will escalate to SRE if this is a systemic rate-limiter attribution issue.

2026-03-12 17:18 UTC - Customer (Claire Montoya, SignalForge): Confirming SDK v2.4.1. Uploaded pcap to s3://support-attachments/SUP-501999/sf-pcap-0312.pcap. Failures consistently include sf-req-20347, sf-req-20356, sf-req-20399. We see higher failures when mixing 'interactive' and 'background' headers on same HTTP/2 connection.

2026-03-12 19:02 UTC - Eng triage (Liam Chen): Reproduced locally with a test harness that emits x-client-priority variations. Initial hypothesis: edge proxy maps priority values to a route tag that uses separate token buckets; when multiple buckets share a connection, refill coordination can lead to one bucket draining and returning 429s for part uploads. Adding debugging flags on ep-usw-3 to capture per-stream bucket attribution.

2026-03-13 02:10 UTC - SRE (Marta Ivanov): We've enabled additional debug logs for rate-limiter on host ep-usw-3-7 for window 2026-03-13T01:50-02:00Z. Observed sequence: a single refill epoch assigned most tokens to 'interactive' lane; background-lane streams were immediately shorted and returned 429s. Investigating token refill policy (epoch ordering) and HTTP/2 stream-to-route mapping race.
2026-03-14 09:30 UTC - Support (Asha Patel): Customer, we recommend two immediate mitigations (below). Eng is preparing a config patch; we'll update once validated in staging.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 - Repro harness: created a client that opens one HTTP/2 connection and alternates x-client-priority header per stream. Observed deterministic 429s when background streams exceeded 25% of concurrent streams.

2026-03-12 - Edge proxy behavior: proxy classifies by header value into lanes 'interactive' and 'background'. Each lane maintains a token bucket. On a shared connection, lane selection occurs at stream start; token buckets are refilled on a per-host epoch. If epoch aligns with heavy interactive traffic, background lane can get zero tokens until next epoch -> immediate 429s.

2026-03-13 - Rate-limiter code review: found a race where the edge calculates per-stream token use based on mapped lane but uses a global refill pointer. If streams are created concurrently with mixed lanes, the refill accounting may favor the lane processed first in the batch allocation loop.

2026-03-13 - Metrics: ep-usw-3-7 showed 4x higher reject-rate for background-lane streams between 23:00-00:30 PDT matching customer imports. Token refill epoch length is 1s; slot assignment loop processes 'interactive' lanes first due to map iteration order.

2026-03-13 - Hypothesis: combination of HTTP/2 multiplexing + per-lane token buckets + non-deterministic lane iteration leads to transient starvation for less-favored lanes on the same connection, producing observed 429s.

2026-03-13 - Tentative fix: change allocation loop to randomize lane ordering per epoch and add per-connection fairness caps so any one lane cannot consume more than X% of tokens in an epoch. Also consider making priority headers advisory (weighting) instead of strict separate buckets for multipart upload route.

2026-03-14 - Staging validation: patched edge-proxy to round-robin lane allocation per epoch and add per-connection min-reserve tokens for lanes. Synthetic repro tests show 0% 429s for background streams at same concurrency levels.
2026-03-14 - Risk assessment: low-risk kernel-level changes, moderate risk to throughput if min-reserve set too high. Will require gradual rollout and canary to Dedicated and Hosted clusters.
resolution: 2026-03-14 - Workaround provided to customer: (1) Set x-client-priority to 'interactive' only for small latency-sensitive calls; use absence of header for bulk parts OR (2) reduce per-connection concurrency to 8 streams for mixed-priority jobs. Both approaches eliminated 429s in their validation runs.

2026-03-14 - Deploy plan: merged PR 2481 to staging. Changes: randomized lane allocation per refill epoch, per-connection reserve 10% tokens per registered lane, and a feature flag to treat x-client-priority as advisory weighting for multipart route. Will monitor reject-rate and latency on staging for 48h before canary to prod-us-west.

Follow-ups: (a) Add console visibility for per-lane reject-rate (ticket INT-88765), (b) Docs update recommending SDK default behavior for multipart uploads (no x-client-priority or 'bulk' value), (c) Product decision on whether priority header should map to separate buckets or weights (product review scheduled).
